title: Windows Update Stack Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper link resolution before file access ('link following') in Windows Update Stack allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025 systems.
factors.exploitability: A local attacker with low privileges and no user interaction can exploit improper link resolution in the Windows Update Stack.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are listed for affected Windows and Server 2025 products, with no exact service-disable or vendor workaround documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation grants SYSTEM privileges, enabling broad local confidentiality, integrity, and availability compromise.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft reports exploitation detected and CISA KEV is true, overriding the low EPSS value of 0.631 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not describe the exploit's file-system prerequisites or whether any supported configuration blocks the vulnerable path.
factors.workload_context: The issue affects current Windows endpoints and Server 2025, including Server Core, and privilege escalation can convert an existing foothold into full system control.

risk_communication.summary: An attacker who already has low-privilege local access can reach SYSTEM through the Windows Update Stack, and exploitation is confirmed.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Confirmed exploitation and full SYSTEM impact require immediate patching regardless of the moderate CVSS score or local prerequisite.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Generic EDR and ASR are not quantified as blocking this link-resolution exploit, and ordinary segmentation does not remove an attacker already local to the host.
reassessment_triggers: Verified installation of the applicable security update
Microsoft or CISA exploitation-status change
Validated exact-path vendor workaround

title: Windows Advanced Local Procedure Call (ALPC) Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows ALPC allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker who can execute code in a low-privilege AppContainer could exploit this vulnerability locally to escape the sandbox and elevate privileges on the affected system. No additional user interaction is required.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows 10 and Windows Server products, with security updates available.
factors.exploitability: An attacker with code execution in a low-privilege AppContainer can locally exploit the ALPC heap overflow without further user interaction.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates KB5122876, KB5122882, KB5122878, KB5123099, KB5123065 and KB5123066 are supplied; no exact path-blocking workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation escapes the AppContainer and grants SYSTEM privileges, creating high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft reports exploitation detected and CISA KEV is present, while EPSS is only 0.572 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The affected product, AppContainer exposure and patch state are customer-specific, but the active-exploitation evidence is explicit.
factors.workload_context: The vulnerability affects Windows endpoints and servers through a local operating-system broker rather than an identified public network service.

risk_communication.summary: A low-privilege AppContainer process can exploit a local ALPC heap overflow to escape its sandbox and obtain SYSTEM privileges.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Confirmed exploitation and KEV listing require Immediate remediation even though the attack is local and requires low privileges.
risk_communication.control_limitations: No generic EDR, ASR, application-control or network control is credited because the record does not identify a tested prevention rule or removable delivery path; controls cannot replace patching.
reassessment_triggers: Verified installation of the applicable security update
Microsoft or CISA changes to exploitation status
Vendor-documented ALPC mitigation that blocks the vulnerable operation

title: CMS AuthEnvelopedData Processing May Accept Forged Messages

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The trigger is forged CMS AuthEnvelopedData, but no configuration is provided to disable that message type or require an alternate validation path.
The vector is network-based, but no listening service or message-delivery route is identified; ACL credit depends on verifying every route to affected OpenSSL consumers.
AV:N does not establish public exposure, and the advisory does not identify an Internet-facing CMS endpoint.
Monitoring may identify malformed CMS processing or suspicious application behavior, but generic EDR does not validate forged messages or prevent their acceptance.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Visual Studio and Azure Linux edk2/OpenSSL products.
factors.exploitability: The CVSS vector permits unauthenticated network delivery with low complexity and no user interaction; exploitation depends on an affected consumer processing forged AuthEnvelopedData.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are listed for Visual Studio and CBL-Mariner packages; no exact protocol-disablement workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Acceptance of forged messages can produce high confidentiality and integrity impact, with no availability impact in the CVSS record.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation status is unknown, KEV is false, and EPSS is 0.435%, below 1%; likelihood is therefore plausible rather than elevated.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not identify the consuming service, required CMS usage, message trust context, or whether affected products expose a network processing interface.
factors.workload_context: Potential impact spans developer tooling and Azure Linux cryptographic consumers, with risk concentrated where CMS AuthEnvelopedData is accepted from untrusted sources.

risk_communication.summary: A vulnerable CMS implementation may accept forged authenticated-enveloped messages, allowing data disclosure or integrity compromise where the message type is used.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The severity is Critical and the unauthenticated network trigger has broad CVSS prerequisites, but no exploitation evidence or concrete service exposure is supplied; out-of-cycle remediation is justified for critical technical risk.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Perimeter controls cannot address internal or application-mediated delivery, and generic monitoring cannot restore message authenticity. Only updating or a verified exact protocol workaround addresses the flaw.
reassessment_triggers: A CMS AuthEnvelopedData consumer is confirmed on a reachable system
A public exploit or KEV listing appears
Microsoft documents protocol disablement or changes the affected-product guidance

title: Microsoft Discovery Studio Information Disclosure Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper neutralization of special elements in data query logic in Microsoft Discovery Studio allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Why are there no links to an update or instructions with steps that must be taken to protect from this vulnerability?

This vulnerability has already been fully mitigated by Microsoft. There is no action for users of this service to take. The purpose of this CVE is to provide further transparency.

Please see Toward greater transparency: Unveiling Cloud Service CVEs for more information.

factors.applicability: Microsoft explicitly states that Microsoft Discovery Studio has already been fully mitigated and requires no user action.
factors.exploitability: The original path was network-based with low complexity, no privileges, and required a user to interact with attacker-controlled query content.
factors.remediation_context: No update or customer remediation is provided because Microsoft states that the hosted service mitigation is complete.
factors.technical_impact: The recorded impact is high confidentiality loss with no integrity or availability impact and changed scope.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation status is unknown, no KEV listing is present, and EPSS is 0.666 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The record does not describe the service-side mitigation or provide customer-verifiable deployment details.
factors.workload_context: The affected workload is Microsoft Discovery Studio, a Microsoft-managed service rather than a customer-patched component.

risk_communication.summary: Microsoft reports a Discovery Studio query-logic information disclosure issue that has already been fully mitigated in the service.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Defer and review is required by the explicit no-customer-action statement, regardless of the recorded technical severity.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Customer controls are not a substitute for Microsoft’s service-side mitigation and cannot independently verify its internal completeness from this record.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft advisory revision
New customer-action guidance
Evidence of residual exposure or exploitation
Disclosure of a customer-managed affected component

title: Microsoft SQL Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: No assessment credit: CVE-2026-65669: least_privilege_pam cannot reduce likelihood when privileges required is none. Model rationale before validation: The exploit requires a user to submit crafted instructions to SQL Copilot, so limiting access to SSMS, Copilot and connected database permissions can reduce eligible workflows, but does not remove the flaw for authorized users.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper neutralization of special elements in output used by a downstream component ('injection') in SQL Server allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to submit specially crafted instructions to SQL Copilot in SQL Server Management Studio. Successful exploitation could bypass intended read-only restrictions and allow database data to be accessed or modified using the connected user's permissions. User interaction is required.

guardrail_adjustments: CVE-2026-65669: least_privilege_pam cannot reduce likelihood when privileges required is none; unsupported mitigation credit removed.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for SQL Server Management Studio 22.
factors.exploitability: The CVSS score is 9.6 with network access, low complexity and no privileges, but user interaction is required; Microsoft explains that a victim must submit specially crafted instructions to SQL Copilot.
factors.remediation_context: An SSMS 22 release update is provided; no exact workaround or service-disable guidance is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can bypass intended read-only restrictions and access or modify database data using the connected user's permissions.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation Less Likely; KEV and detected exploitation are absent, and EPSS is 0.743%.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory's CVSS privileges-required value conflicts with the FAQ's authorized-user SQL Copilot workflow, so practical reachability depends on exposed Copilot usage and connected permissions.
factors.workload_context: The vulnerable component is an administrative client workflow, and impact follows the permissions of the connected SQL account.

risk_communication.summary: A user induced to submit attacker-crafted SQL Copilot instructions may bypass read-only restrictions and alter or read database data.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The Critical score and high impact justify out-of-cycle treatment, while required user interaction and low threat evidence do not establish immediate exploitation urgency.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Generic network segmentation does not mitigate the authorized-user Copilot workflow; access restrictions reduce eligible users but do not patch the injection flaw.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft clarifies the CVSS and authorized-user prerequisite
Exploitation or weaponized Copilot instructions are reported
Verified removal of SQL Copilot or affected SSMS workflow

title: Microsoft Dynamics 365 On-Premises Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The documented deserialization attack requires an authorized low-privilege network user, so strong authentication and restrictive access to Dynamics 365 can reduce the pool of accounts able to reach the vulnerable workflow, subject to bypass-route validation.

notes.value: Deserialization of untrusted data in Microsoft Dynamics 365 allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for Dynamics 365 On-premises version 9.1.
factors.exploitability: The network attack has low complexity and no user interaction, but an authorized low-privilege attacker is required.
factors.remediation_context: A Dynamics 365 security update is available; no vendor workaround or service-disable guidance is supplied.
factors.technical_impact: Successful deserialization can execute attacker code with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact on the Dynamics server.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, there is no KEV listing or detected exploitation, and EPSS is 0.925 percent, below the one-percent likelihood threshold.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not describe the precise authorized workflow, exposed endpoint or account permissions needed beyond low privilege.
factors.workload_context: An on-premises business application server may be shared across users and integrations, increasing the consequence of server compromise.

risk_communication.summary: An authorized low-privilege network user can submit untrusted serialized data to Dynamics 365 and obtain code execution on the server.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Critical impact and a low-complexity authenticated exploit justify out-of-cycle remediation even though Microsoft reports low prospective exploitation likelihood.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Authentication controls reduce eligible attackers but cannot address a compromised authorized account or the vulnerable deserialization logic, and no path-blocking workaround is documented.

KEV listing or EPSS reaching one percent

title: Skype for Business Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

products.name: Skype for Business Server Subscription Edition CU1

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Removing all public ingress to Skype for Business can reduce opportunistic unauthenticated requests, but this receives credit only after every Internet-facing route is verified and does not address internal access.
Restrictive ACLs can reduce reachability to the affected Skype servers only if all relevant lateral and administrative paths are blocked and tested; AV:N alone does not prove Internet exposure.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: External control of file name or path in Skype for Business allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability over the network by sending a specially crafted request that writes an attacker-controlled file to an arbitrary location on the affected server. Successful exploitation could result in the attacker executing code on the target server. No authentication or user interaction is required.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for Skype for Business Server 2015, 2019 and Subscription Edition releases listed.
factors.exploitability: An unauthenticated attacker can send a specially crafted request with low complexity and no user interaction to write an attacker-controlled file to an arbitrary server location.
factors.remediation_context: Updates 5123300, 5123287 and 5123301 are available; no exact service-disable or workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Writing and executing an attacker-controlled file can produce remote code execution with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, there is no KEV listing or detected exploitation, and EPSS is 0.543 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not establish which network interfaces or deployments are reachable, and the arbitrary-file write path may depend on server configuration not described in the record.
factors.workload_context: Skype for Business Server is a shared communications and identity-related service whose compromise may affect many users and integrations.

risk_communication.summary: An unauthenticated network attacker can write a crafted file to an arbitrary location on a Skype server and execute code there.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The pre-authentication, no-interaction exploit path and severe shared-server impact warrant out-of-cycle action despite the absence of current exploitation evidence.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Perimeter removal does not stop an attacker with in-network access, and segmentation is effective only when every lateral and administrative route is blocked; neither control repairs the file-write flaw.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft exploitation status changes
KEV listing or public exploit evidence
Verified exposure of a Skype listener
Verified exact service disablement or complete route isolation

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to an affected SQL Server and submitting a specially crafted query or request that triggers a memory corruption condition, allowing the attacker to execute code on the server. Authentication is required; user interaction is not required.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires updates for SQL Server 2019, 2022, and 2025 CU and GDR branches.
factors.exploitability: The attack is network based with no user interaction and low privileges, but high complexity requires specific protocol or configuration conditions before memory corruption succeeds.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are available and no exact workaround or service-disable guidance is provided.

factors.uncertainty: The specific protocol settings or configurations required for the high-complexity condition are not identified.
factors.workload_context: SQL Server is shared infrastructure where code execution can affect database data, credentials, and dependent services.

risk_communication.summary: An authenticated SQL user may trigger a configuration-dependent memory corruption flaw and execute code on the server.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The critical remote-code-execution impact merits out-of-cycle remediation even though authentication, high complexity, and low threat evidence reduce likely exploitation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Least privilege reduces eligible accounts but cannot block an authorized account that meets the SQL prerequisite, and no generic network control is proven to remove the required configuration.

title: Windows Routing and Remote Access Service (RRAS) Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Removing and verifying all public ingress to RRAS reduces exposure only where every Internet-facing path is removed; the advisory confirms a network packet path but does not establish Internet exposure.

Restrictive ACLs can limit crafted packets to RRAS if all client, partner and lateral paths are identified and tested, but they do not block an explicit in-network attacker by perimeter controls alone.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Remote Code Execution in Windows Routing and Remote Access Service (RRAS) allows attacker to gain an unauthorized access to victim's machine

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted packet to an affected service over the network. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the target system. No authentication or user interaction is required.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Missing authorization in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

The attacker would be able to take over the mailboxes of all Exchange users, attackers can send emails, read emails, download attachments.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker authenticated to an affected Exchange server as a member of a highly privileged role group could send a specially crafted request over the network to bypass mailbox authorization checks. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to access or modify another user's mailbox content without user interaction.

Are the updates for the Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac currently available?

The security update for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 are not immediately available. The updates will be released as soon as possible, and when they are available, customers will be notified via a revision to this CVE information.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

Yes, the Preview Pane is an attack vector.

taxonomy_normalizations: user-content from model-assigned content-delivery tag or preventive content-control judgment

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Microsoft 365, Office, PowerPoint, and Mac LTSC products.
factors.exploitability: The network vector is low complexity with no privileges, but a user must open crafted content; the Preview Pane is also an attack vector.
factors.remediation_context: An update is available for most listed products, but Microsoft states Mac LTSC 2021 and 2024 updates are not immediately available.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation provides remote code execution with high confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact.

factors.workload_context: PowerPoint is widely deployed on endpoints and the Preview Pane can process attacker content without the ordinary open-file action.

risk_communication.summary: Crafted PowerPoint content, including Preview Pane processing, can lead to endpoint code execution.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The Critical severity, broad endpoint exposure, and Preview Pane path justify out-of-cycle remediation despite low current threat evidence.
risk_communication.control_limitations: File filtering depends on recognizing the content route, and Protected View is not proven to block Preview Pane exploitation; Mac LTSC lacks an immediately available update.

Microsoft reports exploitation

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow an attacker the ability to gain remote code execution via an in-network attacker calling arbitrary endpoints.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows client and server products and provides security updates and rollups.
factors.exploitability: The heap overflow is network-reachable with low complexity, no privileges and no user interaction, but Microsoft limits the described route to an in-network attacker calling arbitrary endpoints.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and monthly rollups are listed, with no exact RNDIS disablement or vendor path-blocking workaround documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can provide remote code execution with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.

factors.workload_context: RNDIS is an OS networking component spanning endpoints and servers, but the explicit in-network prerequisite makes internal topology central to exposure.

risk_communication.summary: An in-network attacker may call vulnerable RNDIS endpoints and obtain remote code execution without authentication or user interaction.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The 9.8 pre-authentication technical severity and explicit internal attack path justify out-of-cycle remediation even though current threat evidence is weak.

title: Spring Cloud Azure Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper authentication in Spring Cloud Azure allows an unauthorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An unauthenticated attacker could use an identity token issued by a tenant they control to sign in to an affected multi-tenant application. Successful exploitation could give the attacker an authenticated session and access to protected resources and operations in the target application. No user interaction is required.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain an authenticated session in an affected application from an unauthorized tenant. The attacker could then access protected data and perform actions available to authenticated users in the target application.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for applications using the affected Spring Cloud Azure component.
factors.exploitability: An unauthenticated network attacker can use a token issued by a tenant they control to sign in to a vulnerable multi-tenant application, but specific protocol or configuration conditions are required.
factors.remediation_context: Spring Cloud Azure starter version 7.4.0 and its release notes are provided as the remediation; no separate exact path-blocking workaround is stated.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation creates an authenticated session from an unauthorized tenant, enabling access to protected data and operations available to authenticated users.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation more likely, there is no KEV listing or detected exploitation, and EPSS is 0.643%.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not specify which multi-tenant configurations satisfy the high-complexity conditions or how application authorization is mapped after sign-in.
factors.workload_context: The affected workload is Spring Cloud Azure identity integration in multi-tenant applications, where trust-boundary failure can expose protected application resources.

risk_communication.summary: A token from an attacker-controlled tenant may bypass tenant authorization and create an authenticated session in a vulnerable multi-tenant application.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The critical identity-boundary impact and Microsoft More Likely assessment justify out-of-cycle remediation even though AC:H and low EPSS limit evidence of widespread exploitation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Generic segmentation or stronger authentication does not remove the vulnerable tenant-validation path when the attacker can present a valid token from their own tenant; application authorization must be fixed by the component update.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft or the vendor clarifies affected multi-tenant configurations
Exploitation or KEV evidence appears
The application is verified as single-tenant or the vulnerable component is removed

title: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Incomplete comparison with missing factors in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could convince a user to open a specially crafted Visual Studio Code workspace. The workspace could cause Visual Studio Code to connect to an attacker-controlled service and bypass Workspace Trust restrictions. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to access local data or execute code in the context of the user. User interaction is required, but the user does not need to trust the workspace.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could bypass the Visual Studio Code Workspace Trust feature, allowing content from an untrusted workspace to run commands or code without the user first granting trust. See Workspace Trust for more information.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, a successful exploitation could lead to a scope change (S:C). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

In this case, a successful attack can break out of the Visual Studio Code Workspace Trust feature. See Workspace Trust for more information.

The advisory supplies no EDR-specific behavior for the Secure Kernel heap overflow or kernel-code execution.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Secure Kernel Mode allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability could execute code in the kernel.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for the listed Windows client and Server products.
factors.exploitability: A high-privileged local attacker can exploit a Secure Kernel heap overflow without user interaction; the vector shows low complexity once that privilege exists.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are available, with no documented workaround or supported feature disablement.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation allows code execution in the kernel, with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact across scope.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation Less likely; KEV and confirmed exploitation are absent, and EPSS is 0.325 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not explain how Secure Kernel protections or configuration affect exploitability beyond the high-privilege prerequisite.
factors.workload_context: This is a Secure Kernel post-compromise escalation affecting a broad set of Windows endpoints and servers.

risk_communication.summary: A highly privileged local attacker may use a Secure Kernel heap overflow to execute code in the kernel.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Out-of-cycle remediation reflects Critical kernel impact despite the high privilege prerequisite and only plausible threat likelihood.
risk_communication.control_limitations: PAM reduces the chance of acquiring the required privileged state, but no generic endpoint control is proven to block kernel exploitation or replace the update.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft changes the exploitation assessment
KEV listing or exploitation evidence
Vendor workaround for the Secure Kernel path
Evidence of compromise at kernel level

title: Windows Services for NFS ONCRPC XDR Driver Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Disabling Services for NFS could remove the vulnerable driver path, but Microsoft gives no disablement guidance and the record does not establish whether the NFS service can be safely stopped.

notes.title: FAQ

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

title: Windows Deployment Services Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Deployment Services allows an authorized attacker to execute code locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is local (AV:L). Why does the CVE title indicate that this is a remote code execution?

The word Remote in the title refers to the location of the attacker. This type of exploit is sometimes referred to as Arbitrary Code Execution (ACE). The attack itself is carried out locally. This means an attacker or victim needs to execute code from the local machine to exploit the vulnerability.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, privileges required is low (PR:L). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Any authenticated attacker could trigger this vulnerability. It does not require admin or other elevated privileges.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires updates for affected Windows 10 and Windows Server 2012 through 2025 products.
factors.exploitability: Despite the RCE title, Microsoft states the attack is local, requires code execution on the machine and any authenticated attacker, and has low attack complexity with no user interaction.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and monthly rollups including KB5122876, KB5122882, KB5122871 and KB5123099 are listed; no exact path-blocking workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: The heap overflow can provide arbitrary code execution with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact on the local system.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation more likely, with no detected exploitation or KEV listing and EPSS 0.312 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The title and Microsoft FAQ differ in terminology: RCE describes attacker location, while CVSS and FAQ describe a local execution path.
factors.workload_context: Windows Deployment Services affects server workloads across legacy and current server releases, but the stated trigger is not remote service exploitation.

risk_communication.summary: An authenticated local attacker can execute arbitrary code through Windows Deployment Services and potentially take full control of the host.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Critical impact combined with Microsoft’s More Likely assessment supports out-of-cycle remediation even though the CVSS attack vector is local.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Network exposure controls do not address a local execution path, and generic endpoint controls are not evidence of blocking this specific buffer overflow.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft clarifies or changes the attack path
Exploitation is detected or the CVE enters KEV
Deployment Services is verified disabled under Microsoft guidance

title: Windows Hello Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Microsoft identifies an attacker with OS administrative control or control of a face-sensor adapter; restricting administrative access can reduce one prerequisite, but it does not address a compromised sensor adapter.
The advisory describes the Windows Hello Face secure sensor adapter path but provides no guidance that disabling Windows Hello or the sensor adapter safely removes the vulnerable path.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Hello allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain Virtual Trust Level 1 (VTL1) privileges.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker with administrative control of the operating system, or control of a face-sensor adapter, could submit malformed face data to the Windows Hello Face secure sensor adapter. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code across the VTL0-to-VTL1 security boundary. User interaction is not required.

factors.workload_context: The affected Windows Hello component spans endpoints and Windows Server 2019, with security-boundary impact concentrated on systems using the vulnerable feature.

notes.title: Description

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is network (AV:N) and the attack complexity is low (AC:L). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

The attack vector is Network (AV:N) because this vulnerability is remotely exploitable and can be exploited from the internet. The attack complexity is Low (AC:L) because an attacker does not require significant prior knowledge of the system and can achieve repeatable success with the payload against the vulnerable component.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with explicit permissions could exploit the vulnerability by logging in to the SQL server and could then elevate their privileges to sysadmin.

According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to an affected SQL Server and submitting a specially crafted query or request that triggers a memory corruption condition, allowing the attacker to execute code on the server. notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to an affected SQL Server and submitting a specially crafted query or request that triggers a memory corruption condition, allowing the attacker to execute code on the server. Authentication is required; user interaction is not required.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected SQL Server 2025 CU8 and GDR products.
factors.exploitability: An authenticated attacker can send a crafted query or request over the network without user interaction; CVSS requires low privileges and low complexity.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates 5122770 and 5122769 are provided, and no vendor workaround or service-disable path is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Heap-based memory corruption can yield remote code execution with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact after authentication.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft assesses exploitation as unlikely, with no exploitation detected or KEV listing and EPSS 0.675 percent.
factors.uncertainty: Actual SQL Server exposure, authentication configuration and reachable network paths are customer-specific.
factors.workload_context: SQL Server is shared server infrastructure where compromise could affect hosted databases and dependent applications.

risk_communication.summary: A user who already has SQL Server access can trigger a crafted request that corrupts memory and execute code on the database server.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The impact is severe but exploitation requires authenticated access, Microsoft reports unlikely exploitation, and the EPSS score is below one percent, supporting scheduled patching with access controls as conditional reduction.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Authentication and segmentation reduce eligible paths only when completely enforced; neither prevents exploitation by an authorized account nor removes the need to install the update.

notes.value: Improper access control in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
I am running SharePoint Server 2016. Do the updates for SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 also apply to the version I am running?

Yes. The same KB number applies to both SharePoint Server 2016 and SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016. Customers running either version should install the security update to be protected from this vulnerability.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker who holds site-management permissions on a SharePoint site could start a site export operation that does not correctly enforce permission checks on that site's sub-sites. This could allow the attacker to access content and security-related information from sub-sites they are not otherwise authorized to view. Network access and authentication are required; user interaction is not required.

notes.value:
There are multiple update packages available for some of the affected software. Do I need to install all the updates listed in the Security Updates table for the software?

Yes. Customers should apply all updates offered for the software installed on their systems. If multiple updates apply, they can be installed in any order.

title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Microsoft states that exploitation requires an authenticated attacker with low-level list permissions; restricting SharePoint authentication and permissions can reduce eligible callers when all access paths are covered.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper access control in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
I am running SharePoint Server 2016. Do the updates for SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 also apply to the version I am running?

Yes. The same KB number applies to both SharePoint Server 2016 and SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016. Customers running either version should install the security update to be protected from this vulnerability.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level, list-level permissions on a SharePoint site could submit a specially crafted event receiver definition that causes the server to load an attacker-specified code library and construct an attacker-specified type before the server has verified that the caller is authorized to do so. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code on the SharePoint server. Network access and authentication are required; user interaction is not required.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
There are multiple update packages available for some of the affected software. Do I need to install all the updates listed in the Security Updates table for the software?

Yes. Customers should apply all updates offered for the software installed on their systems. If multiple updates apply, they can be installed in any order.

title: Windows Kernel Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The vulnerability is described as network-based but requires low privileges and user interaction; ACLs can reduce lateral reachability only when all relevant paths are blocked and tested.
Removing unnecessary low-privilege access can reduce eligible attackers because PR:L is required, but it cannot address retained authorized users or the race-condition exploit.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Use after free in Windows Kernel allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows client and Server products.
factors.exploitability: A network attacker needs low privileges and user interaction and must win a race condition, making exploitation difficult but not impossible.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and applicable rollups are listed; no exact kernel-path workaround or service disablement is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can grant SYSTEM with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation more likely; there is no KEV listing or detected exploitation, and EPSS is 0.636%.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not identify the network protocol or conditions that allow a remote attacker to induce the kernel race.
factors.workload_context: The Windows kernel is widespread across endpoints and servers, but AV:N does not establish Internet exposure.

risk_communication.summary: Microsoft rates a network-reachable Windows Kernel privilege-escalation flaw more likely to be exploited; success requires low privileges, user interaction and a race condition.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The elevated Microsoft threat signal and SYSTEM impact justify out-of-cycle remediation despite the difficult exploit prerequisites.
risk_communication.control_limitations: ACLs and privilege reduction depend on complete path and account validation and cannot reliably stop retained users or kernel exploitation.
reassessment_triggers: KEV listing or confirmed exploitation
Microsoft revises the exploitation assessment
A tested vendor workaround that removes the kernel trigger

title: Windows Network File System Denial of Service Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The attack is network-based and requires low privileges plus user interaction; ACLs can reduce reachable NFS paths only if every client and lateral route is verified.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Out-of-bounds read in Windows Network File System allows an authorized attacker to deny service over a network.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows NFS products.
factors.exploitability: A low-privilege network attacker needs user interaction and low-complexity exploitation to trigger the out-of-bounds read.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and monthly rollups are listed, with no documented NFS workaround or service-disable instruction.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can deny NFS service with high availability impact and no stated confidentiality or integrity impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, no KEV or detected exploitation is reported, and EPSS is 0.807%, supporting Plausible likelihood.

factors.workload_context: NFS can support shared file services, so a successful denial of service may affect multiple dependent workloads.

risk_communication.summary: A low-privilege network attacker may disrupt Windows NFS after the required user interaction.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Patching is required, but user interaction and no active exploitation evidence make Scheduled remediation proportionate to the stated availability risk.
risk_communication.control_limitations: ACLs may reduce reachable NFS paths but do not address permitted internal users or impact after exploitation.
reassessment_triggers: Confirmed exploitation or KEV listing
Microsoft clarification of the interaction prerequisite
Verified NFS disablement or complete route restriction

title: Windows SMB Server Denial of Service Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The vulnerability is network-based, so ACLs that block every relevant SMB path, including lateral movement, can reduce attackers able to exhaust resources.
Removing verified public ingress to SMB reduces Internet-origin attempts, but AV:N does not prove Internet exposure and in-network attackers remain in scope.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Allocation of resources without limits or throttling in Windows SMB Server allows an authorized attacker to deny service over a network.

factors.applicability: Microsoft marks customer action required for affected Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2022/2025 products.
factors.exploitability: A low-privilege network attacker can trigger unbounded SMB resource allocation without user interaction or high complexity.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates KB5122882, KB5122878, KB5122871, KB5124008, KB5122880 and KB5124012 are listed.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can exhaust SMB server resources and cause high availability impact without stated confidentiality or integrity loss.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft assesses exploitation as unlikely, but EPSS is 1.09 percent, raising the framework likelihood to at least Plausible; no KEV listing is present.
factors.uncertainty: The record does not state the required SMB request pattern, throttling behavior or whether a service-level workaround exists.
factors.workload_context: SMB Server is shared file-service infrastructure on supported Windows endpoints and Server systems.

risk_communication.summary: A low-privilege network attacker may exhaust SMB Server resources and interrupt file-service availability.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The availability impact affects shared infrastructure and EPSS exceeds one percent, supporting out-of-cycle remediation despite Microsoft's unlikely assessment.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Perimeter filtering does not stop in-network attacks, and ACL effectiveness depends on blocking every SMB and lateral path.
reassessment_triggers: Confirmed resource-exhaustion exploit
KEV listing or higher EPSS
Verified SMB service disablement or vendor throttling guidance

title: Microsoft Exchange Server Tampering Vulnerability

products.name: Microsoft Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Microsoft states that any authenticated attacker can trigger the authorization bypass; strong authentication and access restriction can reduce account compromise if all Exchange authentication paths are covered.
No admin privilege is required, so limiting unnecessary Exchange accounts and permissions can reduce eligible attackers but cannot prevent tampering by a valid permitted user.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Authorization bypass through user-controlled key in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an authorized attacker to perform tampering over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of integrity (I:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker could replace valid file content with specially crafted file content.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, privileges required is low (PR:L). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Any authenticated attacker could trigger this vulnerability. It does not require admin or other elevated privileges.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for supported Exchange Server products.
factors.exploitability: Any authenticated low-privilege attacker can exploit the network authorization bypass without user interaction and with low complexity.
factors.remediation_context: Exchange security updates KB5121608 through KB5121611 are listed, with no exact workaround or feature disablement documented.
factors.technical_impact: An attacker can replace valid file content with crafted content, causing high integrity impact without stated confidentiality or availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, no KEV or detected exploitation is reported, and EPSS is 0.591%, supporting Plausible likelihood.
factors.uncertainty: The record does not identify which Exchange file content can be replaced or the operational scope of tampering.
factors.workload_context: Exchange is shared messaging infrastructure, so unauthorized file modification could affect multiple users or service functions.

risk_communication.summary: Any authenticated Exchange user may bypass authorization and replace valid server file content with crafted content.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The prerequisite is broad among Exchange users and integrity impact is high, but exploitation is not reported and Microsoft rates it less likely; Scheduled patching is supported.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Identity controls reduce account misuse but do not stop a valid authenticated user from reaching the vulnerable authorization path.
reassessment_triggers: Evidence of malicious content replacement
Confirmed exploitation or KEV listing
Verified removal of the affected Exchange file operation

notes.value: Uncontrolled recursion in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for supported Exchange Server products.
factors.exploitability: An attacker needs no privileges or user interaction and can trigger uncontrolled recursion over the network with low complexity.

factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can deny Exchange service with high availability impact and no stated confidentiality or integrity impact.

factors.uncertainty: The record does not identify the vulnerable request route or whether Exchange instances are publicly or internally reachable.
factors.workload_context: Exchange is commonly shared messaging infrastructure, so service failure could affect organization-wide mail operations.

title: Microsoft Exchange Server Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

products.name: Microsoft Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Exploitation requires a low-privilege account with an assigned mailbox, so reducing unnecessary mailbox assignment can reduce eligible attackers, although it does not protect required mailbox users.
The attacker is already authenticated with a mailbox and the advisory gives no evidence that MFA or stronger authentication prevents Exchange token-validation abuse.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Missing authorization in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker with a low-privilege user account and an assigned mailbox, could exploit weaknesses in how Exchange validates requests and identity tokens to impersonate another user. By doing so, the attacker could then access mailboxes through Exchange services as if they were that user.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited the vulnerability?

The attacker would be able to take over the mailboxes of all Exchange users, attackers can send emails, read emails, download attachments.

taxonomy_normalizations: user-content from model-assigned content-delivery tag or preventive content-control judgment

factors.applicability: Microsoft marks customer action required for Exchange Server 2016 CU23, Exchange Server 2019 CU14/CU15 and Subscription Edition RTM.
factors.exploitability: A low-privilege network user with an assigned mailbox can exploit authorization and identity-token validation weaknesses without user interaction or high complexity.
factors.remediation_context: Exchange security updates KB5121608, KB5121609, KB5121610 and KB5121611 are listed, with update links and support references.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can impersonate users and access all Exchange mailboxes, including reading, downloading attachments and sending email; availability is not stated as impacted.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft assesses exploitation as less likely, with no detected exploitation or KEV listing and EPSS 0.707 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not identify the affected request or token flow, and the breadth of mailbox takeover may depend on Exchange configuration.
factors.workload_context: Exchange is shared identity and email infrastructure, so one compromised mailbox account may create broad enterprise confidentiality and integrity exposure.

risk_communication.summary: A low-privilege mailbox user may abuse Exchange identity validation to impersonate users and access all mailboxes.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The shared-service blast radius is high, but the attack requires an authenticated mailbox user and has limited threat evidence, supporting scheduled remediation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Mailbox restriction does not protect legitimate mailbox users, and stronger authentication is not credited without evidence that it gates the vulnerable token path.
reassessment_triggers: Evidence of active mailbox takeover
Microsoft exploitation-status change
Exchange-specific workaround or configuration guidance

title: Microsoft Exchange Server Information Disclosure Vulnerability

products.name: Microsoft Exchange Server Subscription Edition RTM

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The CVSS path requires no privileges and the FAQ says the attacker first obtains a valid encrypted authentication cookie through a separate compromise; stronger authentication is not documented as gating this Exchange inference path.

Exchange network reachability is required for repeated inference requests, so restrictive ACLs may reduce reachable paths if every relevant Exchange and lateral route is blocked and tested; they do not undo a stolen cookie or block an attacker with access.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Use of a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm in Microsoft Exchange Server allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

Exploiting this vulnerability could allow the disclosure of credentials.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires an attacker to first obtain a valid encrypted authentication cookie through a separate compromise and then make repeated requests to infer the protected credentials. These additional prerequisites make exploitation difficult and time-consuming.

taxonomy_normalizations: user-content from model-assigned content-delivery tag or preventive content-control judgment

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for Exchange Server 2016 CU23, Exchange Server 2019 CU14/CU15 and Subscription Edition RTM.
factors.exploitability: The network path requires no privileges or user interaction, but high complexity because the attacker must first obtain a valid encrypted authentication cookie and make repeated requests to infer credentials.
factors.remediation_context: Updates KB5121608, KB5121609, KB5121610 and KB5121611 are listed; no cryptographic workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can disclose credentials, producing high confidentiality impact without stated integrity or availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft assesses exploitation as less likely; there is no KEV listing or detected exploitation, and EPSS is 0.444%.
factors.uncertainty: The FAQ adds prerequisites not reflected by the no-privilege CVSS metric, creating a material availability-versus-prose interpretation caveat for the attack path.
factors.workload_context: Exchange is shared email and identity-adjacent infrastructure, but AV:N does not itself establish Internet exposure.

risk_communication.summary: An attacker who already stole an encrypted Exchange authentication cookie may make repeated requests to infer protected credentials.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Credential disclosure is consequential, but the separate-compromise prerequisite, time-consuming inference and low threat evidence support scheduled remediation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: ACLs cannot protect an attacker with a valid reachable path, and stronger authentication is not shown to gate the already-stolen-cookie prerequisite.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft reconciles the CVSS no-privilege vector with the cookie prerequisite
KEV listing or confirmed exploitation
Evidence that inferred credentials enable direct account takeover

title: Microsoft Windows Media Foundation Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Microsoft explicitly states that exploitation requires a user to open a specially crafted attacker-supplied file, so blocking that file-delivery route can reduce likelihood when coverage is verified.
The advisory confirms crafted-file opening but does not state that Protected View or macro hardening prevents the Media Foundation parser from processing the malicious content.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Windows Media Foundation allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is network (AV:N) and user interaction is required (UI:R). What is the target context of the remote code execution?

This attack requires a user to open a specially crafted file from the attacker to initiate remote code execution.

taxonomy_normalizations: user-content from model-assigned content-delivery tag or preventive content-control judgment

factors.applicability: Microsoft marks customer action required for affected Windows client and Server products.
factors.exploitability: The heap overflow requires no privileges but depends on a user opening a specially crafted file supplied over a network path.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates KB5122876, KB5122882, KB5122878, KB5122871, KB5124008, KB5122880 and KB5124012 are listed.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation provides remote code execution with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft assesses exploitation as less likely, with no detected exploitation or KEV listing and EPSS 0.767 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The record does not identify the media format, delivery channels or whether all applications invoking Media Foundation are covered by filtering.
factors.workload_context: Media Foundation is present across supported Windows endpoints and Server 2019/2022/2025 systems.

risk_communication.summary: A user who opens an attacker-supplied crafted media file may trigger remote code execution through Media Foundation.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The file-triggered impact is high, but required user interaction and limited threat evidence support scheduled patching with delivery filtering as a supplement.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Filtering must cover every file-delivery route, and generic Protected View or macro policy is not shown to prevent this media parser flaw.
reassessment_triggers: Identification of additional media-delivery paths
Confirmed exploitation or KEV listing
Microsoft guidance validating a parser-specific prevention control

title: Windows Spaceport.sys Information Disclosure Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The attack is network-based and requires an authenticated low-privilege caller; restrictive ACLs can reduce access to the affected hosts when every relevant internal path is blocked and tested.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Out-of-bounds read in Windows Spaceport.sys allows an authorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

The type of information that could be disclosed if an attacker successfully exploited this vulnerability is Kernel memory read - unintentional read access to memory contents in kernel space from a user mode process.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for the listed Windows client and server products.
factors.exploitability: A low-privilege authorized attacker can use a network path with low complexity, but user interaction is required.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are available through the listed KB packages; no vendor workaround removes the vulnerable path.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can disclose kernel memory from a user-mode process, creating high confidentiality impact without integrity or availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, with no detected exploitation or KEV listing and EPSS 0.841%.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not define the required user interaction or the network service route used to reach Spaceport.sys.
factors.workload_context: The affected component spans widely deployed Windows endpoints and servers, but AV:N does not establish public exposure.

risk_communication.summary: An authenticated low-privilege network attacker who completes the required interaction may read kernel memory.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The network path and confidentiality impact warrant patching, while required authentication and interaction, low EPSS and less-likely exploitation support scheduled action.
risk_communication.control_limitations: ACLs help only when all internal routes are verified; they do not protect an authorized user who can still reach the vulnerable path.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft changes the exploitation assessment
KEV listing or confirmed exploitation
Discovery of a broadly reachable Spaceport.sys network route

title: Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) Information Disclosure Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The network exploit requires low privileges and no user interaction; strong authentication and restrictive access to AD CS can reduce which authenticated identities reach the vulnerable service, subject to bypass-path validation.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Use of externally-controlled format string in Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) allows an authorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could view heap memory from a privileged process running on the server.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows and Windows Server releases running AD CS.
factors.exploitability: An authenticated low-privilege attacker can send crafted externally controlled format-string input over the network with low complexity and no user interaction.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates KB5122876, KB5122882, KB5122871, KB5123099 and applicable monthly rollups are listed; no vendor workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation exposes heap memory from a privileged AD CS process, causing high confidentiality impact without stated integrity or availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft assesses exploitation as unlikely; KEV and detected exploitation are absent, and EPSS is 0.875%, below the one-percent likelihood threshold.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not identify the exact AD CS endpoint, exposed data selection or whether all deployments expose the same vulnerable request path.
factors.workload_context: AD CS is an identity infrastructure service, so disclosed privileged-process memory may contain sensitive certificate-service or host information.

risk_communication.summary: An authenticated network attacker may disclose privileged-process heap memory from AD CS.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The identity-service context and high confidentiality impact warrant patching, while unlikely exploitation and the low-privilege prerequisite support scheduled remediation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Authentication controls only reduce reachability for unauthenticated or insufficiently authorized identities; they do not prevent abuse by an allowed account or remove the vulnerable parser.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft changes the exploitation assessment
KEV or public exploitation evidence appears
The AD CS endpoint is verified disabled or Microsoft publishes a path-specific workaround

title: Windows NDIS Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Use after free in Windows NDIS allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ

An attacker could use this vulnerability to elevate privileges from Medium Integrity Level to Local Service.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to win a race condition.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for the listed Windows client and server products.
factors.exploitability: A low-privilege authorized network attacker must induce user interaction and win a high-complexity race condition.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and monthly rollups are available; no exact NDIS workaround is documented.

title: Microsoft OpenSSH for Windows Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

If OpenSSH is publicly exposed, removing all public ingress reduces external delivery; AV:N alone does not prove Internet exposure and the required user interaction remains.

notes.title: Description

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability requires an attacker to have a deep understanding of the system. Successful exploitation is not guaranteed and depends on a combination of factors that might include the environment, system configuration, and the presence of additional security measures.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows client and server products.
factors.exploitability: The use-after-free is network reachable without privileges but requires high complexity and user interaction.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are available and no vendor workaround or service-disable instruction is supplied.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can execute code with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.

title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Spoofing Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: A tested WAF rule that blocks the malicious SharePoint upload or generated-page route could reduce delivery, but the advisory supplies no vendor rule and authenticated alternate routes must be covered.
The attack requires an authenticated user to upload malicious content, so restricting upload-capable accounts can reduce eligible attackers, while the required victim interaction remains.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R) and privileges required is Low (PR:L). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

This means an authenticated user can upload malicious content, but exploitation only occurs if they convince another user to visit or interact with that content.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
I am running SharePoint Server 2016. Do the updates for SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 also apply to the version I am running?

Yes. The same KB number applies to both SharePoint Server 2016 and SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016. Customers running either version should install the security update to be protected from this vulnerability.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
There are multiple update packages available for some of the affected software. Do I need to install all the updates listed in the Security Updates table for the software?

Yes. Customers should apply all updates offered for the software installed on their systems. If multiple updates apply, they can be installed in any order.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customers running affected SharePoint Server products to install the listed update.
factors.exploitability: An authenticated low-privilege user uploads malicious content, then must persuade another user to visit or interact with it.
factors.remediation_context: Update 5002908 is available, and Microsoft says all applicable packages for the installed software should be applied.
factors.technical_impact: The cross-site scripting issue is scored for high confidentiality and integrity impact but no availability impact, with spoofing as the stated effect.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, with no KEV listing and EPSS of 0.649%.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not identify the exact content route or whether a WAF can safely block it without bypasses.
factors.workload_context: This affects SharePoint Server Subscription Edition and user-facing collaboration content.

notes.value:
I am running SharePoint Server 2016. Do the updates for SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 also apply to the version I am running?

Yes. The same KB number applies to both SharePoint Server 2016 and SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016. Customers running either version should install the security update to be protected from this vulnerability.

notes.value:
There are multiple update packages available for some of the affected software. Do I need to install all the updates listed in the Security Updates table for the software?

Yes. Customers should apply all updates offered for the software installed on their systems. If multiple updates apply, they can be installed in any order.

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Filtering could help only if it blocks the specially crafted data before delivery, but the advisory describes paste or import into Access rather than a specific email or web-file route.
A tested prevention capability for the Access stack-overflow behavior could help, but generic EDR presence is not sufficient evidence.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Stack-based buffer overflow in Microsoft Office Access allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could provide specially crafted data and convince a user to paste or import it into an affected application. Successful exploitation could allow the attacker to execute code in the user's context.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for Microsoft 365 Apps, Access 2016 and Office 2019/2021/2024 products.
factors.exploitability: An attacker needs no privileges but must convince a user to paste or import specially crafted data into Access; the Preview Pane is explicitly not an attack vector.
factors.remediation_context: Microsoft lists security updates and release-note references, with no workaround that removes the paste/import path.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation executes attacker code in the user's context with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation Less Likely; KEV and confirmed exploitation are absent, and EPSS is 0.878%.
factors.uncertainty: The exact data-delivery channel and user workflow are not specified, and Preview Pane exposure is expressly excluded.
factors.workload_context: This is an Office endpoint risk concentrated on systems with affected Access functionality and a user willing to import data.

risk_communication.summary: Crafted data can execute code when a user pastes or imports it into Access; Preview Pane does not trigger this issue.
risk_communication.why_this_action: User interaction and the less-likely exploitation assessment reduce expected reach, while code execution in the user context still requires normal Office remediation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Content filtering may miss manually transferred data, and generic Protected View or macro policies are not shown to prevent this Access paste/import parser path.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft exploitation-status change
Evidence of a specific delivery channel
Validated Access-specific prevention
Security-update deployment failure

title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Spoofing Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The advisory explicitly requires an authorized attacker with SharePoint administrator privileges; strong authentication and restricted administrator access can reduce access to that prerequisite, subject to bypass-route validation.

The exploit requires the administrator to send a malicious site and convince a victim to open it; filtering or blocking the specific malicious site path can reduce delivery, but it is not a substitute for patching.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper neutralization of input during web page generation ('cross-site scripting') in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
**According to the CVSS metric, user interaction is required (UI:R) and privileges required is high (PR:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

An authorized attacker with administrator privileges must send a victim a malicious site and convince them to open it.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
I am running SharePoint Server 2016. Do the updates for SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016 also apply to the version I am running?

Yes. The same KB number applies to both SharePoint Server 2016 and SharePoint Enterprise Server 2016. Customers running either version should install the security update to be protected from this vulnerability.
