factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for SharePoint Server Subscription Edition; the FAQ also states the same update principle for SharePoint Server 2016 variants.
factors.exploitability: A SharePoint administrator must send a malicious site and persuade a victim to open it, matching network access, high privileges and required user interaction.
factors.remediation_context: Security update KB5002908 is listed; no workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful XSS spoofing can cause limited confidentiality and integrity loss in the victim context, with no availability impact.

risk_communication.control_limitations: Authentication restrictions do not remove the XSS defect, and filtering can miss administrator-delivered or internal content; victim interaction remains a central prerequisite.

title: Windows exFAT File System Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The CVSS attack vector is network and requires low privileges; ACLs can reduce reachable exFAT attack paths only when all relevant network and lateral routes are blocked and tested.
The attacker must be authorized with low privileges, so removing unnecessary access can reduce the prerequisite, though it does not correct the exFAT flaw.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Out-of-bounds read in Windows exFAT File System allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows client and server products.
factors.exploitability: A network attacker needs low privileges and user interaction; attack complexity is low, but the advisory does not establish Internet exposure.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are available and no exact workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation can elevate to SYSTEM with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation Unlikely, with no KEV listing, no detected exploitation and EPSS 0.768%.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not explain the network file-system route or how user interaction is induced.
factors.workload_context: The vulnerable exFAT component spans endpoints and servers, with risk dependent on the specific network-accessible file-system workflow.

risk_communication.summary: An authorized network attacker may use a crafted exFAT interaction to obtain SYSTEM privileges.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The high post-exploitation impact is moderated by required authorization, user interaction and weak threat evidence.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Network controls do not help if lateral paths remain, and reducing privileges cannot protect systems where the attacker retains the required access.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft changes the exploitation assessment
A reachable exFAT network route is confirmed
Public exploitation or a vendor workaround appears

title: Windows DHCP Server Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow an attacker the ability to gain remote code execution via an in-network attacker calling arbitrary endpoints.

risk_communication.why_this_action: The shared-server impact warrants patching, while high complexity and Unlikely exploitation support scheduled rather than emergency handling.
risk_communication.control_limitations: ACLs must cover all internal and lateral paths and do not reduce impact after compromise; perimeter removal receives no credit for this in-network path.

title: Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) Tampering Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The FAQ states that exploitation requires authentication, so strong authentication and access restrictions can reduce access to the AD CS vulnerable path when all bypass routes are covered.
The CVSS vector requires low privileges, so restricting permissions on certificate-service operations can reduce eligible attackers and limit unauthorized modifications.

notes.value: Incomplete list of disallowed inputs in Active Directory Certificate Services (AD CS) allows an authorized attacker to perform tampering over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What could an attacker achieve by exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker could exploit this vulnerability to make unauthorized modifications to protected system data. This could allow the attacker to alter system state or configuration beyond their normal privileges.

notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, privileges required is low (PR:L). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

The attacker must be authenticated to be able to exploit this vulnerability.

factors.remediation_context: Security updates and monthly rollups are available, and no exact AD CS configuration workaround is documented.

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:

An attacker who controls a signed DNS zone could cause an affected DNS server to accept forged DNS records for a different zone as valid. This could cause clients to trust DNS data that did not originate from the authoritative zone.

Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise for 64-bit Systems

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The attack requires a user to open a crafted Word document, but the advisory does not establish email or web delivery or identify a filter rule that blocks the relevant document.
The advisory confirms that Preview Pane is not an attack vector but does not state that Protected View prevents the buffer over-read.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Buffer over-read in Microsoft Office Word allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could potentially read small portions of stack memory.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Is the Preview Pane an attack vector for this vulnerability?

No, the Preview Pane is not an attack vector.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
Are the updates for the Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac currently available?

The security update for Microsoft Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 are not immediately available. The updates will be released as soon as possible, and when they are available, customers will be notified via a revision to this CVE information.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Microsoft 365, Office and Word products.
factors.exploitability: An unauthenticated attacker must convince a user to open and interact with a crafted document; the vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R.
factors.remediation_context: Update 5002923 and Office security-release references are listed, but Office LTSC for Mac 2021 and 2024 updates are not immediately available.
factors.technical_impact: A successful buffer over-read may expose small portions of stack memory, producing high confidentiality impact without stated integrity or availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation Unlikely; KEV and detected exploitation are absent, and EPSS is 0.868%, below the 1% threshold.
factors.uncertainty: The Mac LTSC fix is unavailable at this revision, and the precise document-delivery route and stack-memory contents are unspecified.
factors.workload_context: The issue affects user-operated Word on Windows and Mac endpoints and requires document opening and interaction; Preview Pane is explicitly excluded.

risk_communication.summary: A user who opens and interacts with a crafted Word document may disclose small portions of stack memory.
risk_communication.why_this_action: User interaction, limited stated impact and low threat evidence support scheduled remediation, with a separate exception for Mac LTSC versions lacking an immediate update.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Filtering and Protected View cannot be credited without proving that they block this exact document path and memory-disclosure behavior; Preview Pane is not a mitigation target because it is not an attack vector.
reassessment_triggers: Release of the Mac LTSC 2021 or 2024 updates
Microsoft exploitation-status change
KEV listing or EPSS above 1%
Evidence that disclosed stack memory contains sensitive data

title: Windows Kernel Information Disclosure Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The exploit requires an authorized low-privilege attacker and user interaction; reducing unnecessary interactive accounts can reduce the eligible population but does not prevent exploitation by permitted users.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Exposure of sensitive system information to an unauthorized control sphere in Windows Kernel allows an authorized attacker to disclose information over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

The type of information that could be disclosed if an attacker successfully exploited this vulnerability is Kernel memory read - unintentional read access to memory contents in kernel space from a user mode process.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows client and Server products.
factors.exploitability: An authorized low-privilege attacker requires user interaction over a network; the vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates and monthly rollups including KB5122876, KB5122882, KB5122878, KB5122871, KB5124008, KB5122880, KB5124012 and KB5123099 are listed.
factors.technical_impact: The flaw can expose kernel memory contents to a user-mode process, creating high confidentiality impact without stated integrity or availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation More Likely; KEV and detected exploitation are absent, and EPSS is 0.995%, below 1% but Microsoft’s assessment sets Elevated likelihood.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not specify the required interaction or which kernel-memory contents may be exposed.
factors.workload_context: Kernel memory disclosure affects Windows endpoints and servers and may provide information useful for follow-on exploitation.

risk_communication.summary: A low-privilege user who completes the required interaction may read kernel memory from an affected Windows system.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Microsoft’s More Likely assessment drives Elevated likelihood and out-of-cycle remediation despite the moderate CVSS score and lack of confirmed exploitation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Least privilege reduces eligible users but does not eliminate authorized low-privilege access or block the kernel disclosure path.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft exploitation-status change
KEV listing or EPSS above 1%
Evidence of sensitive kernel-memory exposure
Vendor-specific mitigation for the affected kernel path

title: Microsoft Office SharePoint Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Microsoft requires Manage List permissions, so removing that permission from unnecessary accounts can reduce eligible attackers when all equivalent SharePoint authorization paths are covered.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Missing authorization in Microsoft Office SharePoint allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit the vulnerability?

In a network-based attack, an authenticated attacker with Manage List permissions could execute code remotely on the SharePoint Server.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires the SharePoint Server Subscription Edition security update.
factors.exploitability: An authenticated network attacker with Manage List permissions needs no user interaction and faces low attack complexity.
factors.remediation_context: Security update 5002908 is listed; no exact authorization workaround or service disablement is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation provides remote code execution on the SharePoint Server with high confidentiality, integrity, and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation less likely, with no KEV listing or detected exploitation and EPSS 0.796 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not describe alternate permissions that may imply equivalent Manage List capability.
factors.workload_context: SharePoint is a shared collaboration platform, so server code execution could expose or disrupt concentrated enterprise content.

risk_communication.summary: A SharePoint user with Manage List permissions can execute code remotely on the SharePoint Server.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The authenticated permission prerequisite lowers likelihood, but the server-wide RCE impact requires scheduled patching.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Permission reduction may miss inherited or equivalent authorization paths and cannot contain exploitation by users who retain Manage List access.
reassessment_triggers: An unauthenticated or lower-permission path is disclosed
Exploit code or exploitation evidence appears
All equivalent Manage List authorization routes are verified removed

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with low-level access to an affected server could send a specially crafted request to execute code on the server. User interaction is not required.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025 products.
factors.exploitability: An authenticated low-level attacker can send a crafted network request without user interaction and with low complexity.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are listed for the affected Windows releases; no exact workaround or service disablement is documented.

risk_communication.summary: An authenticated low-level attacker can send a crafted request to execute code through Windows Credential Providers.

title: Windows Kerberos Denial of Service Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The vulnerable Kerberos service is network-reachable without authentication; removing all public ingress to the service can reduce unsolicited external attack paths, but does not block internal or lateral attackers.
Restrictive ACLs can reduce network reachability when every relevant Kerberos path, including lateral movement, is blocked and tested; the advisory provides no exact ACL workaround.

notes.value: Null pointer dereference in Windows Kerberos allows an unauthorized attacker to deny service over a network.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025 products and provides security updates.
factors.exploitability: An unauthenticated network attacker can trigger a null pointer dereference with low complexity and no user interaction.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are available, with no vendor-documented service disablement or exact path-blocking workaround.

risk_communication.summary: An unauthenticated network request may crash or disrupt Kerberos, potentially interrupting authentication services.

KEV listing or credible exploitation evidence appears

title: Azure HDInsight Ambari Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: Microsoft states that a Service Operator can invoke the HDFS REBALANCEHDFS custom command; removing that role where unnecessary can reduce access to the command-injection path, but it does not protect remaining operators.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Improper neutralization of special elements used in an os command ('os command injection') in Azure HDInsights allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges an attacker could gain with a successful exploitation?

An attacker with the Service Operator role in Azure HDInsight Ambari can exploit a command injection flaw in the HDFS REBALANCEHDFS custom command to execute arbitrary system commands as the hdfs user on the NameNode.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What action should customers take to address this vulnerability?

Customers should recreate affected Azure HDInsight clusters so they are provisioned with the updated image. The fix is included in the June 29, 2026 Azure HDInsight release, image 2606012120, and later images. For instructions, see Set up clusters in HDInsight with Hadoop, Spark, and Kafka.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customers to recreate affected Azure HDInsight clusters so they receive the updated image.
factors.exploitability: A network attacker must have the Service Operator role and no user interaction; the HDFS REBALANCEHDFS custom command then permits OS command execution as hdfs on the NameNode.
factors.remediation_context: The fix is included in HDInsight image 2606012120 and later, and Microsoft directs customers to recreate affected clusters rather than apply a conventional host patch.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation elevates from the Service Operator workflow to arbitrary system commands as the hdfs user, with high confidentiality, integrity and availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation status is unknown, KEV is absent, and EPSS is 0.719%, below the one-percent elevated threshold.

factors.workload_context: The affected workload is Azure HDInsight Ambari and the NameNode is a shared cluster control component with potentially broad data-plane impact.

title: Visual Studio Code Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: The vulnerable agent makes outbound requests, so restrictive egress ACLs or an allowlist can reduce access to blocked resources if every agent egress and bypass route is covered; this does not remove the parsing flaw.

The exploit uses HTTP request/response smuggling in content processed by the Visual Studio Code agent, but the record does not identify an application route where a WAF rule could reliably block the crafted URL.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Inconsistent interpretation of http requests ('http request/response smuggling') in Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to bypass a security feature over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What security feature could be bypassed by successfully exploiting this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could bypass the network access restrictions enforced for the Visual Studio Code agent, allowing outbound connections to resources that the configured policy is intended to block.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An attacker could influence content processed by the Visual Studio Code agent so that it requests a specially crafted URL. Successful exploitation could bypass configured network restrictions and allow access to resources that the policy is intended to block. User interaction is required to run the agent against attacker-controlled content.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for Visual Studio Code.
factors.exploitability: An unauthenticated attacker must influence agent-processed attacker-controlled content and obtain user interaction to run the agent; the network vector has low complexity.
factors.remediation_context: A Visual Studio Code security update and release notes are listed; no exact workaround is supplied.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation bypasses the agent's configured network restrictions, with high confidentiality and low integrity impact across the changed security scope and no availability impact.

factors.uncertainty: The record does not define the protected resources, agent deployment model or whether egress policy covers all alternate routes.
factors.workload_context: The affected workload is developer endpoints running the Visual Studio Code agent, where attacker-controlled content can influence outbound requests.

risk_communication.summary: Attacker-controlled content processed by the VS Code agent may smuggle HTTP requests and bypass configured outbound network restrictions.

risk_communication.control_limitations: Egress controls can limit reachable destinations only when comprehensively enforced; they do not fix the agent's request interpretation or guarantee protection from allowed resources.

notes.value: Improper neutralization of special elements used in a command ('command injection') in Microsoft Azure CLI allows an authorized attacker to execute code over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does this mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker would need specific conditions to be in place (i.e. particular protocol settings, or configurations, etc.) before an attack could succeed, which reduces the likelihood of widespread or opportunistic exploitation.

How could an attacker exploit this vulnerability?

An authenticated attacker with permission to modify tags on an Azure virtual machine could add a specially crafted tag. title: Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) for Node.js Spoofing Vulnerability

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Authentication bypass by capture-replay in Microsoft Authentication Library (MSAL) for Node.js allows an unauthorized attacker to perform spoofing over a network.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack complexity is high (AC:H). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Successful exploitation requires an attacker to first obtain a valid ID token issued for the victim and the same application, and then replay it through a separate authentication flow. These prerequisites make exploitation more difficult.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What action should customers take to address this vulnerability?

Customers should update the @azure/msal-node dependency in each affected application to version 5.6.0 or a later compatible version. From the application's project directory, run npm install @azure/msal-node@^5.6.0 --save, then rebuild, test, and redeploy the application using the organization's standard deployment process. See the MSAL Node v5.6.0 release notes and the @azure/msal-node package on npm for additional information.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metrics, successful exploitation of this vulnerability could lead to major loss of confidentiality (C:H), and integrity (I:H), but could lead to no loss of availability (A:N). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

Exploiting this vulnerability could allow an attacker to view highly sensitive user information and modify data, but they cannot affect the availability of the service.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customers to update the @azure/msal-node dependency in each affected application.
factors.exploitability: An attacker needs a valid victim ID token for the same application and must replay it through a separate authentication flow; no user interaction or attacker privileges are required once that prerequisite is obtained.
factors.remediation_context: Microsoft explicitly directs customers to update @azure/msal-node to version 5.6.0 or later, then rebuild, test, and redeploy.
factors.technical_impact: Successful capture-replay can expose highly sensitive information and permit data modification, with no stated availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft assesses exploitation as less likely, with no KEV listing or detected exploitation and EPSS 0.434 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The affected application flows, token exposure routes, and compatibility of the fixed dependency require customer verification.
factors.workload_context: The vulnerability affects application authentication workflows and may reach identity-sensitive enterprise data.

risk_communication.summary: A stolen valid ID token can be replayed through a separate MSAL Node flow to spoof the victim and alter or read protected data.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The prerequisite token theft and high attack complexity reduce prospective likelihood, but the identity and data impact justify scheduled dependency remediation.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Generic segmentation or stronger user authentication does not necessarily invalidate a captured token or remove the vulnerable replay flow.

notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows Biometric Service allows an authorized attacker to elevate privileges locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What privileges could be gained by an attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could gain SYSTEM privileges.

factors.remediation_context: Security updates are available, with no exact biometric-service workaround or disablement documented.

risk_communication.why_this_action: The impact is high but the local prerequisite, limited threat evidence and low EPSS support scheduled remediation.

title: Windows NTFS Remote Code Execution Vulnerability

mitigation_candidates.evidence: No assessment credit: CVE-2026-71329: least_privilege_pam cannot reduce likelihood when privileges required is none. notes.title: Description
notes.value: Heap-based buffer overflow in Windows NTFS allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code with a physical attack.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
According to the CVSS metric, the attack vector is physical (AV:P). What does that mean for this vulnerability?

An attacker with physical access to a vulnerable system could insert a specially crafted USB device.

Are there additional attack vectors?

This vulnerability could also be exploited through a local attack vector. An attacker authenticated as an administrator on a vulnerable system could mount a specially crafted virtual hard drive (VHD) to exploit the system. This scenario results in a lower CVSS score which is why the primary attack vector is listed as Physical in our documentation.

guardrail_adjustments: CVE-2026-71329: least_privilege_pam cannot reduce likelihood when privileges required is none; unsupported mitigation credit removed.

EDR may help identify suspicious local access to Task Scheduler, but the advisory provides no exploit-specific detection or prevention behavior.

notes.title: Description
notes.value: Use of uninitialized resource in Windows Task Scheduler allows an authorized attacker to disclose information locally.

notes.title: FAQ
notes.value:
What type of information could be disclosed by this vulnerability?

An attacker who successfully exploited this vulnerability could disclose uninitialized heap memory from a privileged process.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for affected Windows client and Server versions.
factors.exploitability: A local attacker with low privileges and no user interaction can disclose uninitialized heap memory from a privileged Task Scheduler process.
factors.remediation_context: Security updates are listed for the affected Windows versions; no exact path-blocking workaround is documented.
factors.technical_impact: Successful exploitation discloses small or otherwise uninitialized portions of privileged-process memory, affecting confidentiality without stated integrity or availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft rates exploitation unlikely, there is no KEV listing or detected exploitation, and EPSS is 0.396 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory does not identify the disclosed data or whether a specific deployment exposes a practical local attack path.
factors.workload_context: Task Scheduler is an endpoint and server operating-system component, so compromise depends on prior local access rather than network reachability.

risk_communication.summary: A low-privilege local user may read uninitialized memory from a privileged Task Scheduler process.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The exploit requires prior local access and has low current threat evidence, so scheduled patching is appropriate while preserving the confidentiality risk.
risk_communication.control_limitations: Privilege reduction and monitoring may reduce access or improve detection but cannot prevent disclosure by an authorized low-privilege account.
reassessment_triggers: Microsoft changes the exploitation assessment
KEV listing or confirmed exploitation
Evidence that sensitive data is reliably exposed

title: In libxml2 before 2.15.4, xmlFAParsePosCharGroup has an out-of-bounds read, aka an out-of-bounds read in the NXT macro in xmlregexp.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for libxml2 2.11.5-10 on Azure Linux 3.0.
factors.exploitability: The attack is local, requires no privileges or user interaction, and has high attack complexity.
factors.remediation_context: Azure Linux upgrade guidance is provided, with no documented workaround or feature disablement that removes the vulnerable parser path.
factors.technical_impact: The out-of-bounds read is assessed with no confidentiality or integrity impact and limited availability impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation status is unknown; there is no KEV listing or detected exploitation, and EPSS is 0.116 percent.
factors.uncertainty: The advisory record does not identify the consuming application, parser input route, or whether the affected library is used by a security-sensitive workload.
factors.workload_context: This is a library vulnerability in Azure Linux, so practical exposure depends on local processes that invoke the affected libxml2 functionality.

risk_communication.summary: A locally supplied input reaching the libxml2 regular-expression parser may cause a limited availability failure.
risk_communication.why_this_action: Scheduled remediation is appropriate for the low-severity, high-complexity local issue with no exploitation evidence and a vendor upgrade path.
risk_communication.control_limitations: The record identifies no supported control that specifically blocks the local parser invocation; generic EDR, application control, segmentation and backups do not prevent the vulnerable read.
reassessment_triggers: Identification of a directly exposed consuming application
New evidence of remote or user-delivered parser input
Microsoft or upstream libxml2 workaround guidance

title: xmlregexp in libxml2 before 2.15.4 has a NULL pointer dereference in xmlRegNewParserCtxt after a strdup failure, i.e., it does not calculate a string length after NULL checking.

factors.applicability: Microsoft requires customer action for libxml2 2.11.5-10 on Azure Linux 3.0.
factors.exploitability: The NULL pointer dereference requires local access and high attack complexity, with no privileges or user interaction required.
factors.remediation_context: Azure Linux security-update guidance is available, and no vendor workaround or feature-disablement instruction is supplied.
factors.technical_impact: A failed strdup followed by the unchecked NULL use can cause a process crash, producing low availability impact without stated confidentiality or integrity impact.
factors.threat_evidence: Microsoft exploitation status is unknown, no KEV listing is present, and EPSS is 0.116%, providing minimal exploitation evidence.
factors.uncertainty: The record does not identify the consuming process, allocation conditions, service criticality or whether a crash is reliably attacker-triggerable.
factors.workload_context: The affected workload is the libxml2 library on Azure Linux; operational effect depends on which local application invokes xmlRegNewParserCtxt.

risk_communication.summary: A local, high-complexity memory-allocation failure can crash a libxml2-consuming process.
risk_communication.why_this_action: The impact is limited to availability and exploitation evidence is weak, so scheduled remediation is proportionate while still required by Microsoft.
risk_communication.control_limitations: No supplied generic control is proven to prevent the vulnerable parser operation or preserve availability if the consuming process crashes.
